title: PRO-Seq
scope: Illumina PRO-seq explanatory schematic: four parallel single-biotin-NTP run-on reactions and their RNA-to-cDNA library route. Material states below represent corresponding reaction/library streams, not pooling. Catalogue-mentioned alternative run-on formulations and PRO-cap are qualified separately; their unpictured implementations are not reconstructed.

states.label: Chromatin-associated Pol II with nascent RNA
features: Biological target: positions of transcriptionally engaged Pol II; nascent RNA is the chemical substrate.
Figure labels Pol II and Nascent RNA; chromatin icon supplies context, not a nucleosome-processing branch.
Catalogue permits isolated nuclei or permeabilized cells.

Method description, RNA extraction through cDNA sequencing
evidence.quote: The RNA strands are extracted, fragmented, and purified through streptavidin pull-down. Next, 3' adapters are ligated directly to the purified sample before another streptavidin purification step. The 5' ends are repaired using TAP and PNK before ligating 5' adapters. The adapter-flanked RNA fragments are enriched through another streptavidin pull-down process before RT and PCR amplification. The resultant cDNA strands are sequenced from the 3' end.

states.label: RNA 3′-end-derived sequence positions
features: Text-supported readout beyond the final drawn cDNA: reads from the nascent RNA 3′ end provide incorporation-defined positions used to map transcriptionally engaged Pol II at base-pair resolution.
Each single-NTP library has the corresponding common terminal RNA base; genomic alignment associates that RNA end with a transcription site.
Measures polymerases capable of run-on extension, not all Pol II occupancy or mature steady-state RNA abundance.
The measured boundary is the end after run-on incorporation; primary text permits a single or at most a few identical incorporated bases in a single-NTP reaction.

operations.label: Single biotin-NTP run-on. Four reactions with 1 nucleotide each
operations.description: Pol II extends its associated nascent RNA using the supplied biotin-NTP species in each of four separate reactions, producing biotin-labeled RNA 3′ ends. The diagram names one nucleotide type per reaction, not an all-four-NTP mixture.
operations.mechanism: A single or at most a few identical bases can be incorporated; incorporation of the first biotin base inhibits further elongation. This is a run-on incorporation constraint, not an inferred chemical 3′ blocking group.
operations.information_effect: New terminal RNA bases tie an affinity-selectable RNA end to a polymerase capable of extension. The original paper interprets those ends as nucleotide-resolved positions of transcriptionally engaged Pol II.

operations.label: Extract and Hydrolyze
operations.description: Extract the run-on RNA and fragment it by hydrolysis, yielding RNA fragments including a biotin-bearing terminal fragment. The polymerase/chromatin drawing does not proceed into the library.
operations.information_effect: Fragmentation does not retain the intact transcript as the library unit; the labeled 3′-end fragment remains selectable.

operations.label: Bead coated with streptavidin
operations.description: Partition the extracted fragments by binding biotin-bearing RNA to streptavidin-coated beads; pale fragments remain unbound. The retained output changes attachment state and is the fraction routed into subsequent adapter steps.
operations.mechanism: Affinity association between RNA-associated biotin and bead-associated streptavidin.
operations.information_effect: Enriches labeled RNA fragments; survival of affinity selection alone is not proof of perfect biological specificity.

method_scopes.rationale: PRO-Seq and PRO-seq are capitalization aliases here. The schematic has one common route replicated across the four nucleotide-specific reactions, ending in cDNA for each nucleotide. Downstream selection and adapter stages belong to this PRO-seq implementation. Sequencing is supported by text beyond the final drawn material. Catalogue additionally mentions all four biotin-NTPs, or one with additional unlabeled NTPs. These alternatives are not the four separate one-nucleotide reactions drawn. They are acknowledged as alternative formulations only; no separate graph or equivalence of their positional precision is inferred.

unknowns.question: What chemical end group does the unlabelled black terminal square denote? A legend or identified primary schematic would be needed to assign its chemistry; it is preserved only as an observed symbol.
